build_inputs.angles:
1. Lead on this: it cost close to a hundred thousand dollars new and it was built to beat cars at twice the money - that was the whole point of it. Today it is the cheap way into a car that hits 60 in under three seconds. Nothing else at this money is this quick, and it has not got slower.
2. Cover what the engine will take, because that is why these cars are still a bargain. The V6 is hand-assembled and massively over-built: a tune and fuel alone takes it past 600 hp, and one shop has documented 879 hp at the wheels on a completely untouched engine. With bigger turbos the aftermarket runs these well past 1,000 hp, which is Lamborghini and Ferrari territory for the price of a used Camry's worth of parts. The gearbox is what gives up first, not the engine.
3. For the head-to-head use the 2012 Porsche 911 Turbo - the car the GT-R was aimed at, costing far more when both were new, and slower to 60.

title: 2012 Nissan GT-R Premium
youtube_title: Built to humble cars costing twice as much 🔥

history.fact: For 2012, Nissan enlarged the GT-R's front openings to increase airflow through the radiator and improve front-brake cooling.

scenes.headline: 2.9 Seconds
scenes.narration: Built to humble cars costing twice as much, it hit sixty in 2.9 seconds without aftermarket help.

scenes.headline: 2012 Cooling Changes
scenes.narration: The 2012 Nissan GT-R Premium's facelift pushed more air through the radiator and cooled its front brakes.

scenes.headline: Wheel Horsepower
scenes.narration: This modified example makes 634 horsepower and 699 pound-feet of torque after tuning and fueling upgrades. Both measured at the wheels.

scenes.headline: Rear Transaxle
scenes.narration: Its all-wheel-drive system puts the six-speed dual-clutch gearbox behind the cabin to improve weight distribution.

scenes.headline: Remote Exhaust Valves
scenes.narration: That AAM exhaust has remotely operated valves, so you can change its volume without crawling underneath.

scenes.headline: VR38DETT
scenes.narration: Nissan hand-assembles the twin-turbo VR38DETT in Yokohama using plasma-sprayed bores instead of cast-iron liners; Jotech's 1,000-wheel-horsepower builds upgrade both engine and transmission. Stock internals aren't invincible.

scenes.headline: Premium Seats
scenes.narration: The Premium came with heated leather seats, not a factory Nismo seating package.

scenes.headline: $90K → $66K
scenes.narration: They started around $90,000 new; they go for about $66,000 today. Would you buy this much speed instead of a newer car with a warranty?

script: Built to humble cars costing twice as much, it hit sixty in 2.9 seconds without aftermarket help. The 2012 Nissan GT-R Premium's facelift pushed more air through the radiator and cooled its front brakes. This modified example makes 634 horsepower and 699 pound-feet of torque after tuning and fueling upgrades. Both measured at the wheels. Its all-wheel-drive system puts the six-speed dual-clutch gearbox behind the cabin to improve weight distribution. That AAM exhaust has remotely operated valves, so you can change its volume without crawling underneath. Nissan hand-assembles the twin-turbo VR38DETT in Yokohama using plasma-sprayed bores instead of cast-iron liners; Jotech's 1,000-wheel-horsepower builds upgrade both engine and transmission. Stock internals aren't invincible. The Premium came with heated leather seats, not a factory Nismo seating package. They started around $90,000 new; they go for about $66,000 today. Would you buy this much speed instead of a newer car with a warranty?

sections.Highlights: THIS... is a 2012 Nissan GT-R Premium, finished in Deep Blue Pearl with a black interior. The attached Carfax history report lists no mileage discrepancies in this GT-R’s past. It also confirms that this Nissan has been mostly registered in California since new. Factory equipment includes driver-configurable transmission, suspension, and vehicle dynamic control modes, Brembo brake calipers, a body-colored rear spoiler, leather upholstery, heated front seats, a Bose audio system, and cruise control. Modifications reported by the seller are extensive, and the full list is detailed below. Highlights include an AAM Competition valved exhaust system with remote function, AAM Competition 3-inch high flow catted downpipes, AAM Competition upper intercooler pipe kit with twin Tial blow-off valves, an EcuTek ECU tune, Injector Dynamics ID1050X injectors, KW coilovers, 20-inch Vossen Wheels HF-5 wheels, a CarbonTastic steering wheel, and a 14-inch Nifty City head unit with Apple CarPlay capabilities. Called the R35 internally, the GT-R arrived in 2009 as the performance bargain of its decade. It fended off European and American rivals with a hand-built V6 that delivered supercar-like performance, a unique exterior design, an infotainment system developed by the company responsible for the Gran Turismo franchise, and a relatively affordable price tag. Power comes from a 3.8-liter twin-turbocharged V6, rated at 530 horsepower and 448 lb-ft of torque in stock form. According to a dyno sheet pictured in the gallery, this GT-R currently produces 634 horsepower and 699 lb-ft of torque at the wheels. Output is sent to all four wheels via a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission.
